name: Astragalus

project_scope.selection_mode: Six already-canonical Central Texas Astragalus cards; protect strict nativity and variety concepts
project_scope.native_range_note: All six canonical species/variety target-zone decisions were PROVISIONAL before this pass; this visual module does NOT certify any county PASS.
project_scope.taxonomy_note: Recognized A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri and A. nuttallianus var. pleianthus are specific accepted VARIETIES; do not relabel parent species photo as exact variety. A. leptocarpus photo backfill follows separate canonical process.
project_scope.media_scope: Existing physical public-safe photos: A. nuttallianus and A. plattensis. A. lindheimeri exact source CC BY-NC noncommercial study only, not reused in the unrestricted genus; three species without images before batch.

look_here_first: Start with a whole plant showing a PINNATE leaf and irregular PEA flower (upper BANNER, side WINGS, two-part KEEL). Then immediately inspect ONE ripe POD in side view: narrow or fleshy, straight or curved, smooth or hairy, with GROOVES along dorsal/ventral SUTURES? In Central Texas a plump groundplum pod does NOT automatically mean A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri; A. plattensis has an extremely similar pod. On annuals, look at leaflet tips and flower number to separate the A. nuttallianus complex.

genus_diagnostics.flower: Astragalus flowers are papilionoid FABACEAE: five specialized petals including one upper BANNER/STANDARD, two lateral WINGS and a folded lower KEEL. Typically 10 stamens (commonly nine joined, one free) surround a single carpel. Colors range purple-blue to whitish; this is a broad genus cue, not a species key.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Leaves usually ALTERNATE and PINNATE, with numerous paired little LEAFLETS on a RACHIS; small STIPULES may sit at the leaf base. Count leaflets and inspect apex: RETUSE means a shallow notch and distinguishes some closely related Texas annuals when used with flower size.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: A single superior ovary matures as a LEGUME/POD. The broad genus spans narrow straight dry pods, long curved pods, flattened fruit and large fleshy groundplum-like pods. Inspect hair (GLABROUS vs PUBESCENT), ridges/grooves on dorsal/ventral SUTURES, inflation/fleshiness, and inward wall/septum.
genus_diagnostics.pod_sutures: Every legume has dorsal and ventral SUTURES (seams) associated with its single carpel. In A. plattensis mature fruit is grooved along BOTH and carries hairs. A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri commonly lacks the plattensis ovary pubescence. Use a real macro and do not label sutures with arrows before pixel verification.
genus_diagnostics.pubescence: Hair types can be tiny: STRIGOSE means short, stiff, appressed (flattened against surface); PILOSE means longer soft hair; PUBESCENT is a general hairy condition. OVARY HAIRS, not perceived overall greenness or pod thickness, break important groundplum ties.
genus_diagnostics.habit: Both ANNUALS and PERENNIALS occur. Young annuals such as A. leptocarpus, A. nuttallianus and A. lindheimeri may be small spring plants; stout low perennial A. plattensis and A. crassicarpus can both bear fleshy fruit.

study_strategy.look_here_first: Flower → pinnate leaf → mature pod → pubescence on ovary/pod → fruit grooves and leaflet tips
shared_traits: Fabaceae ancestor: one flowering carpel becomes a pod; pea-petal pattern occurs in papilionoid legumes including Astragalus.
Astragalus: alternate pinnate leaf with multiple leaflets, pea-type flowers arranged singly or in racemes, and exceptionally useful pod architecture.
Local tie-breakers: developing ovary/pod hairs for plattensis vs berlandieri; leaflet tips, raceme flower count, and narrow/curved pod shape among small annuals.
priority: 1. SEE an overall plant and flowers with a whole stem including leaf architecture.
2. SPOT the actual developing ovary and photograph pod side + both seams at the same 1-mm scale.
3. NAME banner, wings, keel, leaf rachis, leaflet apex, pod pubescence and dorsal/ventral sutures.
4. COMPARE the two stout groundplums before comparing annual slim pod types.
5. REMEMBER that a broad A. nuttallianus photo does not automatically certify var. pleianthus.
warnings: Do not use groundplum fruit thickness to distinguish A. plattensis from A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri; they overlap.
A. lindheimeri is an annual with flattened curved-oblong pods; earlier provisional 'inflated perennial' descriptions were corrected against reviewed flora.
A. crassicarpus var. crassicarpus Commons images are a different accepted variety, not a substitute for var. berlandieri.
Photos are for learning morphology, not proof of any Hays County presence; all strict range statuses remain unchanged.

quick_key.if: THICK fleshy, rounded/oval green pod low to the ground
quick_key.then: Compare A. plattensis vs A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri. Is the developing OVARY/POD hairy? Check both sutures for grooves.

quick_key.if: Groundplum ovary/pod generally SMOOTH, not pubescent; seams not deeply grooved
quick_key.then: A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri candidate. Needs exact variety source and multi-trait verification.

quick_key.if: Thick fleshy pod with visible fine HAIRS and prominent grooves along both seams
quick_key.then: A. plattensis. The current installed fruit photo can show the general fuzzy plump pod.

quick_key.if: Tiny annual, narrow almost STRAIGHT glabrous pod and retuse/notched leaflet tips
quick_key.then: A. leptocarpus, compare A. nuttallianus complex and inspect larger flowers/longer pod.

quick_key.if: Annual with showy bicolored purple-blue and white flowers, flattened CURVED pod (not thick balloon)
Annual with tiny purple/white flowers, low habit, slender often curved pods
quick_key.then: A. nuttallianus at species group. Do NOT automatically resolve a specific variety.

quick_key.if: A. nuttallianus complex with broader leaflets not all notched and 4–9(–12) flowers per raceme
quick_key.then: A. nuttallianus var. pleianthus candidate; needs a documented exact-variety photo and mature pod key.

quick_key.if: Flowers only; no leaves, mature fruits or identity to variety
quick_key.then: Astragalus sp. (or A. nuttallianus complex) until reproductive characters are mature.

comparison_cards.title: Two thick-podded look-alikes — Berlandier's groundplum vs Platte River milkvetch
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Take photographs of the developing OVARY at high resolution. Are there hairs? Then rotate the mature pod to see both SUTURES. Their similarly fleshy shape is NOT the diagnostic split.

field_matrix.berlandieri: Less conspicuously grooved; verify full literature diagnosis
field_matrix.plattensis: Often deeply grooved on BOTH dorsal and ventral sides

field_matrix.berlandieri: Low perennial; may resemble plattensis in South-Central Texas
field_matrix.plattensis: Perennial spreading stems, sometimes emerging from buried caudex branches; overlaps Berlandier's

field_matrix.berlandieri: Missing exact var. berlandieri (don't use var. crassicarpus substitute)
field_matrix.plattensis: One installed photo of plump fuzzy pods; macro for groove needed

comparison_cards.caution: Rupert Barneby's NYBG treatment explicitly notes sympatry and best difference is ovary pubescence. Never rely on pod thickness alone.

comparison_cards.title: Small annuals — slimpod vs Nuttall's vs var. pleianthus vs Lindheimer's
comparison_cards.look_here_first: First compare blossom size and leaflet TIP; then count FLOWERS PER RACEME and inspect a fully mature pod. Flowers and pods overlap; use a multi-character key.

field_matrix.leptocarpus: often shallowly RETUSE (notched) in documented Texas material
field_matrix.pleianthus: many upper leaflets obtuse to subacute, not all notched
field_matrix.lindheimeri: leaflets in short pinnate leaves; bicolored flower especially useful

field_matrix.leptocarpus: often small racemes 1–2 locally, sometimes more

field_matrix.lindheimeri: curved, flatter in cross-section and larger bicolored flowers

comparison_cards.caution: The Astragalus nuttallianus species page may refer broadly to several varieties. Do not assert an A. nuttallianus photograph also proves var. pleianthus without independent specimen determination.

comparison_cards.title: Fabaceae / Astragalus vs other pea relatives
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Pinnate leaves plus bilateral pea-type flowers signal papilionoid Fabaceae; confirm the solitary fruiting carpel forming a legume and inspect pod form, rachis, stipules and hair type.

field_matrix.traits: Often many paired leaflets on pinnate leaves; pea-type flowers in racemes and pods variable from narrowly linear to fleshy or inflated; species keyed by pod sutures, hair and septum
Often smaller leaflets and clustered fine papilionoid florets in dense spikes, different seedpods
BIPINNATE leaves with subdivided pinnae, globose heads often of many stamens, not conspicuous bilateral milkvetch flowers

comparison_cards.caution: Pea-family relatives overlap on corolla type and compound leaves: identify flowers and mature pods together.

visual_comparison.title: Milkvetches: the best field key is in the POD
visual_comparison.subtitle: THREE physically installed rights-cleared exact-species photographs: A. nuttallianus flowers + narrow pod, A. plattensis thick hairy pods, and A. leptocarpus slender numerous pods. A. lindheimeri existing photo is noncommercial CC BY-NC study only; two accepted Texas varieties still lack exact-variety images.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: LEAVES & FLOWERS get you to Astragalus. POD HAIRS + SUTURE GROOVES split two groundplums. LEAFLET TIPS + FLOWER COUNT + POD SHAPE split little annuals.

part_examples.title: 1 · SEE a real milkvetch pea flower
part_examples.look_for: Look at the conspicuous UPPER BANNER (STANDARD) petal, the two side WINGS and the lower fused KEEL that encloses the stamens/pistil. On the same plant find a PINNATE leaf made of several LEAFLETS. This is a real A. nuttallianus photo, NOT var. pleianthus proof.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Connects the Astragalus genus to the papilionoid branch of Fabaceae. Petal parts overlap many other pea-flowered genera; fruit and stipules narrow the species.

part_examples.title: 2 · SPOT a curved Nuttall's milkvetch pod
part_examples.look_for: Just BELOW the flowers on the real plant, find the pale curving LEGUME. The bending pod is a helpful cue, not by itself a firm split from A. leptocarpus and other variable relatives; leaf-tip shape and flower/raceme size matter.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Learn fruit early: different milkvetches make narrow, long, hooked, inflated and thick fleshy pods.

part_examples.title: 3 · COMPARE a thick hairy groundplum-like pod
part_examples.look_for: These are REAL A. plattensis pods, NOT Berlandier's groundplum. Notice their plump green shape and fine surface fuzz. Check for GROOVES along both pod seams (SUTURES), but the grooves need another calibrated side-on close-up to certify.
part_examples.why_it_matters: For south-central Texas, groundplum and plattensis both make plump pods; the truly useful split is HAIRY versus nearly GLABROUS developing ovary/pod and fruit sutures.

part_examples.title: 4 · NEED EXACT PHOTO — Berlandier's groundplum
part_examples.role: A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri fleshy usually glabrous pod
part_examples.look_for: Find per-photo rights-cleared specimen identified to A. crassicarpus VAR. BERLANDIERI (not typical var. crassicarpus). Photograph whole plant, flower and thick fleshy low pods, then 1-mm ovary hairs to compare with A. plattensis. Known var. crassicarpus Commons photos are NOT exact-subspecies proof.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Avoid mislabeling northern/widespread variety photos as the Texas-specific Berlandier's groundplum card.

part_examples.title: 5 · See REAL slimpod milkvetch narrow pods
part_examples.role: long narrow pod and pinnate leaflets
part_examples.look_for: Look for MULTIPLE narrow, pointed, mostly straight pods held on fine stems against a brown-green ground. Small PINNATE leaflets are visible in the occupied plant. This source is a verified fruit photograph, NOT a matched flowering plant, calibrated pod measurement or retuse-leaflet macro.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Immediate comparison with A. plattensis thick hairy green fruits and with A. nuttallianus narrow curved pod. Flowers and leaf tips still need a matched new macro.

part_examples.title: 6 · NEED PHOTO — Lindheimer's flower and pod together
part_examples.role: bicolored banner wings and flattened curved pod
part_examples.look_for: The existing exact A. lindheimeri species picture shows bicolored purple-blue and white pea flowers, but is CC BY-NC 4.0. Find a rights-cleared matched flowering/fruiting stem with FLATTENED CURVED pods. Do NOT teach swollen balloon pods or perennial habit for this annual.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates A. lindheimeri from nearby small-flowered annual milkvetches without repeating an older provisional science error.

part_examples.title: 7 · NEED PHOTO — A. nuttallianus var. pleianthus
part_examples.role: varietal leaf tips / flowers raceme / glabrous pod
part_examples.look_for: Photograph specimen identified to var. PLEIANTHUS, with 4–9(–12) flowers on raceme, broad leaflets often acute/obtuse at ends and an intact smooth narrow mature pod with calibrated lengths. A genus/species-level A. nuttallianus image cannot certify this variety.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The accepted Texas variety deserves its own photo and explicit comparisons, not duplicate photography falsely labeled as the variety.

part_examples.title: 8 · NEED MACRO — tiny pod hairs and grooves
part_examples.role: pubescent vs glabrous ovary and dorsal / ventral pod sutures
part_examples.look_for: Matched exact-species A. plattensis and A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri developing ovaries under hand lens, plus mature pods cut to show dorsal and ventral SUTURES and inward septum. One 1-mm ruler and same angle.
part_examples.why_it_matters: This specific structural pair is the strongest practical learning target for these otherwise very similar groundplums.

part_examples.title: 9 · NEED MACRO — banner wing keel and compound leaf
part_examples.role: flower dissection / leaflet tips / stipules / pulvinus
part_examples.look_for: A rights-cleared dissected flowering Astragalus photo showing BANNER, WINGS, KEEL and sepals, and a second photo labeling leaf RACHIS, paired LEAFLETS, terminal leaflet if present and basal STIPULES. Add arrows only after verifying actual pixels.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Teaches family → genus anatomy at field scale and makes the vocabulary more memorable.

visual_comparison.annotation_policy: No arrows installed: labeling a very small hair, suture or scale requires verifying target structure and original-pixel coordinates. Missing exact-variety photos are explicit blank tiles.
visual_comparison.photo_rights_notes: A. lindheimeri canonical photo credit Joanne Toler CC BY-NC 4.0, not promoted to public unrestricted genus. Generic A. crassicarpus / var. crassicarpus internet photos not exact var. berlandieri.
